recommendations.title: `test_constraints_prompt_names_every_required_row_key` in `tests/test_roadmap.py` (step 6 "Add the constraints stage wit
recommendations.body: `test_constraints_prompt_names_every_required_row_key` in `tests/test_roadmap.py` (step 6 "Add the constraints stage with the attribute-totality gate and the cross-artifact anchor gate") asserts `key in _constraints_prompt_text()` against the whole prompt, so all 15 required keys stay green even with the entire `## The frontmatter inventory` section deleted from `roadmap-constraints.md` — the embedded YAML example restates every one of them. The check is also substring-loose: 7 of 9 plausible renames (`anchor`→`anchor_id`, `id`→`ids`, `statement`→`statements`, `attribute`→`attributes`, `constraints`→`constraint`, `decisions`→`decision`, `dispositions`→`disposition`) still match existing prompt text and ship green. The detail assigns this test the job of reddening on a rename rather than "silently producing prompts that ask for the old spelling", and it delivers none of it — a prose inventory that asks for `anchor_id` while `parse_constraints_artifact` requires `anchor` costs the stage every attempt and halts the arc, which is the failure this guard exists to prevent. The twin `test_domain_prompt_names_every_required_row_key` / `_required_domain_row_keys()` has the identical hole, so fix both from one helper
recommendations.suggested_action: in `tests/test_roadmap.py`, slice each prompt's `## The frontmatter inventory` section and match each key as a whole token (the `_ID_CHARACTER` boundary pattern in `roadmap_gates.py:_prose_names_id` is the precedent) instead of `key in <whole prompt>` — verified green today for all 15 constraints keys and all 15 domain keys
